_comment: THE REGISTRY, and it is the only source of truth about what this machine can do.
A tool that is not in this file does not exist. The brain is shown the capability
sentences and nothing else; it asks for a tool by id with a control tag; and the id
it names is looked up here EXACTLY - no fuzzy match, no nearest name, no guessing at
a near neighbour. That is the same discipline as the model allowlist, for the same
reason: a machine that guesses which action you meant will one day guess wrong while
holding something sharp.
No key, token or password ever appears here, and none is ever passed to a script. A
tool that needs a credential fetches it itself, server-side - config.json for the
model keys, secrets/google_token.json for the Google grant - and the wire between
this machine and the browser never carries one.
proposal blanks are usually parameter names, but the calendar hand earns two DERIVED
blanks that hands.py composes and the script never receives: {when} and
{duration}, from a start/end pair. They exist so the spoken sentence can
be a human reading of a machine stamp - 'Monday 28 September at 4:00 pm'
rather than '2026-09-28T16:00' - while the rows underneath still show the
employer the exact values that will travel. They are computed from the
validated parameters by the same code the script uses, so the card and the
wire cannot disagree.
An email body has NO such blank, on purpose: `proposal` is spoken out loud,
and preflight check 16(f) plants a canary in that body and fails if it is
ever heard. The body is shown on the card and never read to the room.
Each entry:
id          the name the brain asks for and the ledger counts under. [a-z0-9_-]
name        what a human calls it, shown above the Yes/No pair
script      a bare filename inside tools/ - never a path, never a shell string
capabilities the sentences the brain may match a request against. Write them the
way your employer would say the thing, not the way a manual would.
triggers    regular expressions that decide only ONE thing: whether a message is
worth offering the brain a chance to ask for hands at all. They never
choose a tool - the brain does that, and the id above is checked
exactly. A trigger that is too greedy costs a model call; a trigger
that is too narrow means the hands are never offered.
params      name / type / required. string, text, integer, number, boolean.
Anything not listed here is dropped before the script sees it.
timeout_s   how long it may run before it is killed and reported as failed
proposal    the sentence spoken before anything happens, with {param} blanks.
This is where your voice lives: write it the way you would want to be
asked. It is composed from THIS template and never from model prose,
because a model that paraphrases an action can understate it.
Adding a hand is a ten-line script and four lines of JSON. Nothing else.

tools.name: Write something into the calendar
capabilities: put an appointment, a reminder or a meeting in the employer's calendar
remind the employer to do something at a particular time
book or schedule something for a given day or hour
tools.proposal: That would be '{title}', {when}, {duration}, sir, written into your Google calendar. Shall I put it in?

tools.name: Send an email
capabilities: send an email to somebody on the employer's behalf
write to a person or an address and say something to them
tools.proposal: I have an email ready for {to}, sir, under the subject '{subject}'. The card carries what it says. Shall I send it?
tools.step: Send an email to {to} under the subject '{subject}'.

tools.name: Change the voice he speaks in
capabilities: change the voice the assistant speaks in, to one of the voices installed on this machine
make yourself sound like somebody else - ryan, joe, alan, or the northern one
switch, swap or recast the spoken voice
tools.proposal: You are hearing {current} at the moment, sir. That would make it {voice} from the next word on. Shall I change the voice?

tools.name: Relaunch Chrome with the debugging port
capabilities: open Chrome's debugging port so a focus session can lock a TAB rather than the whole browser
restart the browser with the debugging port when locking a tab is impossible without it
put back the tab-level watching that a browser started without the port cannot do
tools.proposal: I need Chrome relaunched with the debugging port to lock a tab, sir. Shall I?
tools.step: Relaunch Chrome with the debugging port.

tools.name: Bring you back to the locked tab
capabilities: bring the employer back to the tab he locked a focus session on
tools.step: Bring you back to the locked tab.

tools.name: Test the hands themselves
capabilities: prove that the tool machinery itself works, touching nothing at all
tools.proposal: A self test, sir, carrying the token {token} and touching nothing. Shall I run it?
tools.step: Run a self test carrying the token {token}.

tools.name: Save the minutes of a meeting
capabilities: write up the minutes of a meeting the Scribe transcribed and keep them as a note
save minutes that have already been drafted into notes/, under a title like Meeting-2026-09-26-1432
tools.proposal: I have the minutes drafted, sir, to be kept as '{title}'. Shall I save it?

tools.name: Write a thought down as a note
capabilities: write something the employer wants remembered into his own collection as a note
keep a thought, a decision or a fact he has just said, so it can be cited later
leave folder out unless the Census is asking: it is captures unless told otherwise
tools.proposal: That would go into your collection as '{title}', sir, a note of its own. The card carries what it says. Shall I write it down?

tools.name: Make a film public
_why: THE ONLY HAND THAT PUBLISHES, and it is a hand rather than a server route for one reason:
this is the instant a film becomes visible to the world, and the Hands' gate exists to put
a human between this house and an act that strangers can see. The upload itself is NOT a
hand - it takes a minute and lands unlisted, so it runs behind the Doorman with a progress
bus, which is the Director's shape.
EVERY PARAMETER IS A ROW OF THE CHAIN CARD, which is why there are six of them and why
four are only ever read and never used. S40 asks the card to show title, description, tags,
thumbnail and the unlisted URL before the boss says yes - and in this house the card IS the
slot's parameters. So they are parameters: not because the script needs them, but because
approving something invisible is not approving it. publish_video.py uses `video` alone, and
checks even that against the ledger rather than trusting the request.
NO CAPABILITY SENTENCE MENTIONS A TOPIC OR A TITLE, so the brain cannot be led into
proposing this for a film that does not exist: the only legitimate source of a video id is
an upload this machine has already done, and the script refuses any id that is not in its
own ledger.
capabilities: make a film that is already uploaded and unlisted visible to everybody on YouTube
publish, release or go public with the video that was just put up unlisted
tools.proposal: '{title}' is up and unlisted, sir - {url}. The card carries the description, the tags and the thumbnail. Shall I make it public?

tools.name: Draft the newsletter
_why: THE DRAFT, AND IT SENDS NOTHING. This hand composes from the boss's own notes and
reports the shape of what it wrote - how long, how many snippets, which note ids.
It opens no socket. The Director's render is not a hand for the same reason this
one barely needs to be: making a thing is not the act the gate exists for.
IT IS REGISTERED ANYWAY, because the registry is the only way the brain learns a
tool exists, and in this house a registry entry is inseparable from the Chain Card
- hands.propose() builds one for every tool there is. That costs a confirmation on
a harmless act, and it is the right cost: the alternative is a second execution
path that runs scripts without a card, which is the parallel mechanism the mandate
forbids building.
NO CAPABILITY SENTENCE NAMES A SUBJECT OR A SUBSCRIBER, exactly as publish_video's
name no topic: the brain must not be led into drafting for a list that does not
exist, and the only legitimate source of a topic is the boss asking for one.
capabilities: draft a newsletter from the employer's own notes on a subject he names
write up what the notes say about something, as an issue to go out later
tools.proposal: I can draft the newsletter on {topic}, sir, from your own notes. Nothing goes out - it only writes. Shall I?

tools.name: Send the newsletter
_why: THE HAND THAT GOES OUT, and the second one in this house whose work cannot be taken
back. send_email reaches one person; this reaches the whole list, one message each,
and an email cannot be unsent. So it is gated by the Chain Card exactly as
publish_video is, and for the identical reason: the Hands' gate exists to put a
human between this house and an act that strangers can see.
EVERY PARAMETER IS A ROW OF THE CARD, which is why five of them are only ever READ
and never used by the script. publish_video's own law applies without a word
changed - approving something invisible is not approving it - so the subject, the
recipient count, the opening of the body and the cited note ids are parameters: not
because the script needs them, but because a boss approving a send must be able to
read what is being sent. send_newsletter.py uses `topic` alone, and re-reads the
subscriber list and re-composes the body from the notes at send time rather than
trusting anything that travelled on this card.
NO CAPABILITY SENTENCE NAMES A SUBJECT OR A RECIPIENT. The brain must not be able
to propose a send for a newsletter that was never composed, and a capability that
mentioned a subject is an invitation to do exactly that.
capabilities: send the drafted newsletter to everybody on the employer's subscriber list
put the newsletter out to the list that is already on file
tools.proposal: The newsletter on {topic} is ready, sir - '{subject}', going to {subscribers} subscriber(s). The card carries the opening and the notes it cites. Shall I send it?

tools.name: Write an entry into the ledger
_why: THE LEDGER'S PEN, and the one write a chat sentence can reach beyond the other hands.
Every amount in it is the employer's own figure, parsed by the server from what he said
(ledger.parse_request) - never a model's. So it names DOORS: proposed only through the
ledger door the server's own parse uses, never from a [[tool: ...]] tag, never as a step
of a chain, and never described to the brain at all. See hands._clean_tool.
`entry` IS THE SENTENCE THE CARD SPEAKS, composed by ledger.describe() from the other
parameters - and add_ledger_entry.py composes it again from them and refuses to write if
the two differ. What he approved out loud is what goes in the book, to the paisa.
amount_paise is an INTEGER: a ledger has no floats, and the card shows the exact figure
that will be written. proof is 'none' or a path under proofs/ that exists.
capabilities: write an income or an expense the employer has just stated into one of the two books, Galaxy's own running costs or his business's
tools.proposal: {entry}, sir. Shall I write it down?
tools.step: Write an entry into the ledger: {entry}.

tools.name: Void an entry in the ledger
_why: THE LEDGER'S STRIKE-THROUGH. Nothing in the book is ever deleted: a wrong entry is voided,
keeps its row, and gains a reason and a time. Door-bound for the same reason as
add_ledger_entry. `entry` is the existing entry as ledger.entry_line() reads it, and
void_ledger_entry.py reads it again at the moment of writing and refuses if it changed.
capabilities: strike out one entry in the ledger as void, keeping it in the book with the reason the employer gave
tools.proposal: That would strike out {entry}, because: {reason}. It stays in the book, marked void. Shall I void it?

tools.name: Send a WhatsApp message
_comment: Not door-bound: the ordinary propose -> confirm gate, from any door, like send_email.
There is no recipient parameter. The number is meta_whatsapp_to in config.json,
the employer's own, read by the script itself - so the model can choose what is
said and never to whom. And, like send_email, the proposal never speaks {body}:
the body is on the card, verbatim, and a report read aloud to the room is the
same mistake as a letter read aloud to it.
capabilities: send a WhatsApp message to the employer's own phone
tools.proposal: I have a WhatsApp message ready for your own phone, sir. The card carries what it says. Shall I send it?
tools.step: Send a WhatsApp message to your own phone.
